leads.summary: Booking Holdings' Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reportedly discloses that FTC staff notified Priceline in July 2026 of intent to recommend a complaint over allegedly unfair/deceptive hotel-advertising practices (disclosures, fees, customer support, billing). Secondary sources report a $900M revenue reduction and $100M accrued loss recorded in the quarter, with potential FTC-sought restitution/penalties variously reported as "exceeding $1 billion" (Skift) or "above $500 million" (Reuters, per an anonymous source). New this run: secondary reporting now also describes Priceline as being in settlement discussions with the FTC, with no settlement yet reached and litigation still possible; one outlet names the B2B affiliate as "Guest Reservations" (not named in the filing itself per that same reporting).

leads.summary: Expedia Q3 2026 earnings call held 2026-11-04. Secondary coverage (PhocusWire, Zacks, FourWeekMBA, 247wallst, Hospitalitynet) reports: Q3 revenue ~$4.9B (+12% YoY), B2B revenue ~$1.7B (+23% YoY); advertising revenue growth slowed to 7% in Q3 from 13% in Q2, attributed by CFO Derek Andersen partly to AI tooling/campaign-management changes; CEO Ariane Gorin reportedly confirmed participation in OpenAI ad products (via an automated Benzinga transcript quoted by FourWeekMBA) but PhocusWire separately reports she did NOT confirm which specific product, so whether this is 'Sponsored Agents' specifically remains unconfirmed; agentic traffic described as 'still small' but with 'strong purchase intent' per Zacks paraphrase of Gorin. New this run: PhocusWire reports Expedia's integration with Meta's 'Muse' agent was due to go live 'during the call' (i.e. on/around 2026-11-04), which would newly establish Expedia (not just Agoda/Trip.com) as a Muse integration partner -- unconfirmed pending primary source.

leads.summary: Airbnb's Q3 2026 shareholder letter (reported release date 2026-11-05) reportedly sets a first-half-2027 timeline for rolling out Airbnb's own AI travel agent to guests, handling bookings across 'every vertical in travel' within the Airbnb app, plus in-trip assistance. CEO Brian Chesky reportedly rejects a single general-purpose-agent model, and is quoted (via secondary sources) saying general-purpose agents such as Meta's 'Muse' and 'Instinct' generate 'little traffic and even fewer bookings' for Airbnb -- a management claim about competitor products, not independently measured. Sponsored listings reportedly planned only after the agent ships. Separately, Airbnb's AI customer-support tooling reportedly resolved ~40% of support issues without a human agent in Q3 2026, up from about one-third in Q2 2026 (management-reported metric, no independent verification).
